key_insight: Machine learning can identify degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but reliable predictions depend strongly on training-data coverage.
engineering_relevance: Temperature- and illumination-dependent voltage measurements could support post-fabrication diagnosis, while replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor gains.
method: Compare forward surrogate models trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Train a multi-label classifier to detect six degradation mechanisms from open-circuit-voltage measurements.
evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieves macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; on independently sampled devices, XGBoost R² falls to 0.58 with grid training but reaches 0.995 with Latin hypercube training.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, and the diagnostic classifier fails to generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
